records.text: The term "State Police" shall refer to:
(a) The Mayflower State Police
The term "highway" shall refer to:
(a) The entire width between the boundary lines of every way or place of whatever nature when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic
The term “gubernatorial line of succession” shall refer to:

(a) The order in which the other public officers of the state’s government assume the powers and duties of the Governor upon an elected Governor’s death, resignation, removal from office, or incapacity, which shall go as follows:
(i) The Lieutenant Governor
(ii) The President pro Tempore of the State Senate
(iii) The Secretary of State
(iv) The Attorney General
(v) The Chief Justice of the Mayflower Supreme Court
(vi) The Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard

(b) If all offices in the aforementioned list are vacant, or their holder incapable or unwilling to perform the duties of Governor, then the State Senate shall meet for emergency session, and under sealed ballot, elect a new Governor.
The term “other persons protected by the Mayflower State Police” shall refer to:
(a) Any person whom the Mayflower State Police is authorized to protect under law, or by Executive Order of the Governor when such person has not declined protection.
The State Police shall be established at the seat of government and be a principal department in the Governor’s cabinet.
The Governor shall appoint, with the advice and consent of a majority of the Senate, a Colonel.

The Colonel shall be responsible for the management and control of the State Police. The Colonel shall make and adopt rules and regulations for the direction, control, discipline and conduct of the members of the State Police and such other rules for the government and operation of the State Police as he may deem necessary. He shall also designate the authority and responsibility for each rank of State troopers in the State Police. The Colonel shall also:
(a) Issue all medalions for Taxi Operators, and;
(b) Issue all permits for Commercial Aircraft Operators, and;
(c) Issue all permits for Commercial Drivers.
The Colonel shall be subject to removal by the Governor, with cause, legal grounds, or objective reasonableness, or by the Senate through impeachment and conviction.

The State Police shall be responsible for the safety and security of the State’s highways and may enter and secure the safety and enforce the laws of any local subdivision or unincorporated territory. The State Police shall also ensure scene command and investigation for vehicular incidents such as collisions or pursuits, and operate a Tactical Support unit for the emergency needs of the State. The State Police shall further have the authority of carrying out orders of the Supreme Court, as necessary. This paragraph shall not be construed as to limit the jurisdiction of the State Police, which shall have jurisdiction over the entire State, and are not limited in where they may patrol.

The State Police shall serve to provide security and protection to the gubernatorial line of succession, and shall be responsible for determining the security of the State Capitol. The Governor may further direct for certain officials or buildings to recieve the protection of the State Police.

The Colonel shall be responsible for the management and control of the State Police. The Colonel shall make and adopt rules and regulations for the direction, control, discipline and conduct of the members of the State Police and such other rules for the government and operation of the State Police as he may deem necessary. He shall also designate the authority and responsibility for each rank of State troopers in the State Police. The Colonel shall also be granted the statutory authority to:

ADMINISTRATIVE ABILITY. In the event that the protective operations of the Mayflower State Police are running at a suspended, terminated, or reduced capacity then the Major General of the National Guard shall have a contingency plan in place to carry out protective services in accordance with these provisions.
The Colonel of the Mayflower State Police shall have the ability to set policy, rules, and regulations for executive protection operations in accordance with this law.
(a) Any existing law or provision that conflicts with subchapters (IV), (V), or (VI) shall be repealed.

PROTECTIVE ACTION. The Mayflower State Police must provide protective services to members within the Line of Succession to the Governor. This shall include, but not be limited to; the Lieutenant Governor, President pro tempore, Attorney General, and Chief Justice. With the exception of the Secretary of State which falls under the Diplomatic Security Service.
The Mayflower State Police must protect events and functions in which the aforementioned may be in attendance.
The Mayflower State Police shall develop strategy, plans, and operational guidelines to render protective service to the aforementioned.
The Mayflower State Police may request help from the National Guard in providing these protective services.

The State Police shall not protect an aforementioned official if such official refuses service, aside from the Governor of the State of Mayflower. The Governor of the State may not decline protection at any time and under no circumstances, but may request a lesser amount of personnel conducting protection duties. It will be the duty of the State Police to accommodate these requests if made.

Other members of Law Enforcement may not assist in the protection of the individuals mentioned in 3 M.S.C. 1 § 1401 unless specifically requested by the Mayflower State Police through official communications.
The Lee County Sheriff’s Office must provide protective services to the following individuals
(a) Justices of the Supreme Court;
(b) District Court Judges;
(c) Department Heads of County Departments that are on the County Government team;
The aforementioned positions shall have primary protection by the Lee County Sheriff’s Office.
The Lee County Sheriff's Office shall hold authority and priority for the protection of the aforementioned protectees (see 3 M.S.C. 1 § 1409).
The Lee County Sheriff shall oversee the process and organization of protections and protection requests.
In the absence of the Sheriff’s Office, the Mayflower State Police may be authorized to provide protection to (in a temporary capacity), Justices of the Supreme Court.

ZONING STRATEGY. Members of Law Enforcement who are conducting or helping in the act of protections may establish a protective zone no greater than 50 feet (studs) from the protectee, so long as the protectee has the legal right to be on that property and the provider has the legal right to secure that property. No individual who is not an on duty peace officer, government official, or otherwise authorized individual may enter a protective zone.

records.text: No protective zone shall be established on private property without consent from its owner or custodian. If within the confines of a publicly owned building and/or publicly owned property, the protective zone shall extend to the entirety of the building or property, and the reasonable area (approximately ten (10) studs) surrounding such building or property. If within the confines of a privately owned building, the protective zone shall extend the entire size of a reasonable area designated by the State Police (which shall not be larger than one hundred (100) square studs) and a five (5) stud radius around any doors, entryways, or exits. No individual except an on-duty peace officer, government official, or authorized person may enter a protective zone.

records.text: 3 M.S.C. 1 §§ 2201-2205 may be temporarily suspended in the event of a declared state of emergency, as determined by the Governor.

Department head(s) shall have the privilege to petition the Governor, with the advice and consent of a majority of the Senate, to adjust the budget of their respective agencies for the purpose of special necessity, these special necessities including;
(a) Any current, or future authority afforded to them by statutory law, that they cannot fulfill due to current budget constraints.
The Department of Justice shall be responsible for monitoring compliance with the staffing limitations outlined in subchapter (2) of this Chapter.
Any department, whose budget is in violation of the limitations set by the provisions outlined in subchapter (2) of this Chapter shall comply with the following:
(a) Issuing a notice to the Attorney General and the Governor regarding the issue of the department being over-budget.
(b) With the advice of the Attorney General, the department shall develop a plan to restrict employment and recruitment until budget constraints are met.
(c) The department shall terminate employment of individuals to reach their budget, with the advice and consent from the Department of Justice, and Attorney General as needed.
(d) The department shall only begin recruitment once their current employment numbers are under their budget as prescribed by law.

(e) The Attorney General shall have the ability govern the employment status of department employees, excluding department heads, with an at-will exemption from the employee rights prescribed by law; in order to meet department budgets set in this act.
The term “Act of Congress” shall refer to:
(a) A bill or law passed by the Senate of the State of Mayflower and adopted into law notwithstanding the Governor's objection.
The term “Code of Statutes” shall refer to:
(a) The "Mayflower State Code" spreadsheet owned by stateWARE, specifically all of its Titles.
The Community Administrator shall appoint a State Registrar.
(a) No law may be enacted affecting this Subchapter without the consent of the Community Administrator.
(b) The State Registrar shall have the authority to hire assistants as he sees fit.
The State Registrar shall codify all Acts of Congress into the Code of Statutes upon their enactment into law.
The Code of Statutes shall be defined as this Spreadsheet, and shall consist of Titles as proglumated by the State Registrar.
The State Code of Statutes should be cited as [Title] M.S.C. [Subtitle] § [Chapter][Subchapter][Code].
(a) For example, the 55th law in the 6th Title, 2nd Subtitle, 3rd Chapter, 1st Subchapter would be cited as "6 M.S.C. 2 § 3155."
(b) If a Statute uses a part, it should be cited as: [Title] M.S.C. [Subtitle] § [Chapter][Subchapter][Part].[Code].
(i) For example, the 1st law in the 6th Title, 5th Subtitle, 4th Chapter, 3rd Subchapter, 2nd Part would be cited as "6 M.S.C. 5 § 4302.1."
(c) Every code in Title 1 and Title 2 should be cited as: [Title] M.S.C. § [Subtitle][Chapter][Code].
The State Registrar shall organize passed laws into the Code of Statutes in a manner prescribed by policy.
No law, amendment to a law, repealment of a law, or criminal charge shall come into effect until its codification into the Code of Statutes.
(a) The State Registrar shall be mandated to codify any law, amendment, repealment, or charge within 24 hours of its passage by the Governor, notwithstanding extenuating circumstances.

In the event of a conflict between the verbiage or text of an Act of Congress and codification of it Code of Statutes, the Courts are directed to defer to the Code of Statutes in line with Community Administrator directive.
If a code is ever significantly affected by a judicial decision, its status shall change to what is displayed as the status of this code.
The term “State department” and “Department of State” shall refer to:
(a) The Mayflower Department of State.

The State Department shall be the chief clerk of state as prescribed by the Constitution. Responsible for the curation of museums, the registration and regulation of corporations, and the chief diplomat of the State of Mayflower.

The Secretary of State shall be responsible for the management and control of the Department of State. The Secretary of State shall make and adopt rules for the regulation, conduct, and direction of the State department.
The Secretary of State shall create offices within the Department of State as is necessary and proper.
The Secretary of State shall consult with the Governor on all matters relating to the foreign posture of the State, and deliver all messages from the Governor to appropriate foreign representatives.
The State Department shall have a deputy that is able to assume his office if necessary, and perform the duties as acting Secretary of State.

There shall be an Office of Commerce led by an Assistant Secretary of State, overseen by the Secretary of State. This office shall be responsible for the regulation and enforcement of regulation in regard to business entities.
The Secretary of State shall handle the registration of business entities and intellectual property within the State. This power may be delegated to the Commerce Office.
The types of Businesses & Incorporation shall be defined as such:
(a) The term “Sole Proprietorship” shall refer to a business that is owned, headed, and managed by one person who is completely liable for the business.

(b) The term “General Partnership” or “Partnership”shall refer to a business that is managed by a group of members that hold equal say in their business as partners and are jointly responsible for the business’s financial obligations and legal liabilities.
(c) The term “Corporation” shall refer to a business that is managed by a group of people and they choose a board of directors and officers to manage their business.
(i) Corporations shall have the ability to issue stock to raise capital. If the Corporation chooses to do so, then it must be publicly displayed that they do so.
(ii) Corporations shall have regular shareholder meetings if it issues stock.
(d) The term “Limited Liability Company” shall refer to a business that is a Corporation but individual members enjoy personal protection from liability, like lawsuits.
(e) The term “Limited Liability Partnership” shall refer to a business that is a Partnership but individual partners enjoy personal protection from liability, like lawsuits.

(f) The term “Freelance” shall refer to a business owned, operated and managed by an individual who provides services independently, typically on a part-time or per-project basis, without long-term commitments to a single employer or client.
(g) The term “Non-profit” shall refer to a business that exists to further a social cause and/or provide a public benefit where all revenue must go back into the non-profit or into its operations.

(h) The term “Cooperative” shall refer to a business jointly owned and democratically controlled by its members. Business operations are controlled by a Board of Directors elected by general membership vote, who shall carry the burden of its financial obligations and legal liabilities. A cooperative is a type of corporation and its government shall be through its articles of incorporation as filed.

(i) The term “Joint Venture” shall refer to a business in which two or more parties, who shall carry the burden of its financial obligations and legal liabilities, agree to pool their resources to accomplish a specific task or project. Joint ventures can be formed as separate legal entities or as contractual agreements between the parties involved.
A registered business entity can sue or be sued.
The types of Intellectual Property shall be defined as such:
(a) The word “Copyright” shall refer to any original works of creation limited to: literature, graphical design, recordings, films, or broadcasts.
(i) A copyright may not include: ideas, concepts, facts, names, titles or persons.
(ii) A copyright shall expire 6 months after it is registered.
(b) The word "Trademark" shall refer to any distinguishing features of a licensed business, limited to: logos, slogans, sounds, symbols, or word marks.
(i) A trademark may not include: Common words, ordinary shapes, ordinary colours, symbols associated with a good, or sounds associated with a good.
(ii) A trademark shall expire 6 months after it is registered.
The Secretary of State shall create a database which contains all active and inactive business licenses.
The Secretary of State shall create a database which contains all active and inactive intellectual property licenses.

The Secretary of State shall handle the registration of business entities and intellectual properties within the State, ensuring that all necessary documents and information prerequisites are provided on the registration method.

(a) The Secretary of State shall create publicly accessible forms for creating business entities and intellectual property defined in Subchapter IV, with reasonable requirements as the Secretary of State sees fit.

There shall be a publicly accessible document, known as the “Application for Articles of Organization” that shall be made publicly available by the Department of State. The Secretary of State may cosmetically rename this form.
(a) The Secretary of State shall refuse to file an application for articles of incorporation if it does not meet the following standards:
(i) The name of the corporation is clearly typed and designated as such.
(ii) It must contain an initial appointment of the board of directors.
(iii) It must contain the number of authorized shares and who the shares are distributed to.
(iv) The name of the incorporator is clearly typed and designated as such.
(v) It must contain an attached set of bylaws which shall dictate the appointment of the board of directors and the further apportionment or sale of shares.
(b) The Secretary of State shall refuse to file an articles of general partnership if it does not meet the following standards:
(i) The name of the general partnership is clearly typed and designated as such.
(ii) The initial partners.
(iii) Authorization for a majority of partners to modify the general partnership including the admittance or expulsion of partners.
(iv) The designation and appointment of a managing partner.

There shall be a publicly accessible document, known as the “Intellectual Property Registration” that shall be publicly available by the Department of State. The Secretary of State may cosmetically rename this form.
(a) The Secretary of State shall refuse to accept an intellectual property application if it does not meet the following standards:
(i) The owner of the intellectual property is clearly typed and designated as such.
(ii) The type of intellectual property is clearly selected as such.
(iii) It contains a copy of the property that is requested to be declared intellectual property.
(iv) It contains a description of the intellectual property, with all defining features clearly typed and designated as such.
(v) It contains a description of meaning or significance to the property owners.
(b) The Secretary of State shall designate an intellectual property ID to each approved work of intellectual property.
No person shall shall lease or own a commercial property without proper licensing from the Secretary of State.
(a) Any contravention of this code is guilty of violating 1 M.S.C. § 1406.

The Secretary of State may make guidelines towards any registered business entity in the interest of ensuring that fair market practices are maintained, ethical practices are maintained, and that businesses operate within the scope of State law.

(a) The Secretary of State may prescribe guidelines on any consequences to a business entity's license to operate if the business entity is in contravention of any guidelines prescribed under this code.
Owners of intellectual property which attempt to exercise control over their intellectual property may not do so unless the intellectual property contains:
(a) Labelling which clearly shows a work as intellectual property.
(b) Labelling which clearly shows the type of intellectual property.
(c) Labelling which clearly shows the owner of the intellectual property.
(d) Labelling which clearly shows when the work first became intellectual property.
(e) Labelling which clearly shows the intellectual property ID designated to the property by the State Department.
Any business that fails to publicly display that it issues stocks shall be liable for criminal investigation and conviction for 1 M.S.C. § 3106 “Fraud in the first degree.”

No individual shall disclose or share confidential property or information of commercial benefit, where the owner of the trade secret has taken steps to maintain secrecy of the property, of which shall be known as a "Trade Secret."

The Department of State shall incorporate a sub-agency (hereinafter “Division of Public Safety”, "Division" or “DPS”); which shall be the primary protective and security entity of the Department of State. The service shall be considered autonomous from the Department of State.

records.text: The term "Correctional Officers" shall refer to:
(a) Law Enforcement Officers of the Lee County Sheriff's Office.
(b) Civilian employees designated as Correctional Deputies by the Lee Cοunty Sheriff's Office.
The term “Convict” and “Inmate” shall interchangably refer to:
(a) Individuals convicted of a crime and sentenced to a term of imprisonment, or arrested for a set period of time by a sworn peace officer.
The term “Peace Officer” shall refer to:
(a) A person certified by the State by the Law Enforcement Training Institute to, among other things, to carry out warrantless arrests, carry government-owned firearms, and enforce court orders.
The term “Warden” shall refer to:
(a) The employee designated by the County Sheriff to manage all Correctional Deputies.
The term “Contraband” within the meaning of 1 M.S.C. § 1709 shall refer to:

(a) Any item not authorized by facility/warden rules, regulations, or law, including but not limited to weapons, controlled substances, electronic communication devices, escape tools, or any item introduced with the intent to aid in escape, concealment, or disruption of facility operations.
The term “Introduces” within the meaning of 1 M.S.C. § 1709 shall refer to:
(a) Any attempt to bring contraband into a facility through physical delivery, mail, drop-off, or other means.
The term “Manufactures” within the meaning of 1 M.S.C. § 1709 shall refer to:
(a) The alteration, construction, or creation of contraband from permitted items within the facility.

There shall be in a complex known as the Lee County Jail, which shall be located at Rikers Island in Lee County, Mayflower, and which shall consist of the property under the jurisdiction of the Lee County Sheriffs Office.

records.text: Any Court of record may designate law enforcement training institute certified individuals as Probation Officers to execute the responsibilities under this Subchapter.

Probation Officers may conduct warrantless searches of any individual actively on probation or parole, or on pretrial release as specified by court order. These searches must be equally applied to individuals on probation, and may not be targeted unless with probable cause.
Individuals on probation, parole, or on pretiral release as specified by court order:
(a) If arrested, notify the arresting law enforcement agency of their status as a person on probation/parole/pretrial release.
(b) Refrain from posessing or carrying any weapons, including firearms.
(c) Refrain from the commission of further criminal offenses of any level.
(d) Adhere to lawful directions given by Probation Officers, including to meet with the Probation Officer at specified locations and times.
(e) Comply with any searches done by Probation Officers or law enforcement officers.
(f) Refrain from removing any electronic monitoring devices placed on ones person.
(g) Refrain from associating with any individual with 3+ felony records, or who is actively on probation.

records.text: (a) Detain any individual for up to twelve (12) minutes, or until the arrival of a sworn law enforcement officer, whichever occurs first, if the individual fails to comply with a lawful order to leave the Lee County Jail; commits or is suspected of committing a criminal offense (violations of Title 1 of the M.S.C.) within the grounds of the Lee County Jail or immediately adjacent thereto; commits a criminal offense against, within the vicinity of, or in connection with a prisoner work operation or community service operation supervised by Correctional Officers; commits or is suspected of committing a violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1311 Escape anywhere within the State; or if instructed to do so by a sworn law enforcement officer. records.text: Correctional Officers are authorized to use deadly force against a prisoner when the officer reasonably believes such force is necessary to prevent the commission of a violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1311 Escape. This authority is given when the prisoner is confined within a prison, jail, road camp, work operation, or other penal institution, or is being transported to or from such a facility or place, and the officer reasonably believes the prisoner is escaping or attempting to escape from lawful confinement. Deadly force may only be used if the officer has made a reasonable effort, when feasible, to warn the prisoner that deadly force will be used unless the escape attempt ceases immediately and only if the officer reasonably believes that no other means are available to prevent the escape.

records.text: The Chief Medical Examiner shall review, and retain exclusive jurisdiction on, the activity or lack thereof, of public officials and public servants regardless of political subdivision.
The Chief Medical Examiner, or the Medical Review Board, shall launch medical investigations based on reports or suspicions of inactivity from public servants or government officials.

(a) Any individual(s) contracted to assist with a medical investigation shall be temporarily afforded the investigative authority and jurisdiction of the Medical Review Board for the duration of said investigation.
(b) Individuals contracted to a medical investigation may be severed from the investigation at any time, at the discretion of the residing Coroner, or Chief Medical Examiner.

The Chief Medical Examiner, or the Medical Review Board with the consent of the Chief Medical Examiner, shall have the authority to subpoena access to any channel or section of any official Discord server, provided that it is pursuant to an investigation related to their duties, or for the aims of finding any signs of life.
(a) Should any section or channel be classified, said section must remain under seal, viewable only by the Chief Medical Examiner and investigating Medical Review Board.
(b) Any investigating party under the Medical Review Board must provide reasonable justification for the subpoena of information and show that it is relevant to their duties.

(c) The Medical Review Board cannot subpoena access to internal channels or communications without first proving that an individual has been inactive within all public forums for a minimum of thirty days without an excuse of absence.

(d) Any written documentation created or issued by the medical review board that utilizes evidence from channels classified under the State Secrets Act shall only contain the timestamp and author of a communication. Furthermore, no message content that was posted within classified communications shall be present in any written documentation, regardless of redaction.

In drastic circumstances, as so determined by the Chief Medical Examiner, they may issue compulsory warrants, with written signature from a member of the judiciary, for the physical in-game presence of a person, to appear before the Medical Review Board as proof of life.
(a) The Coroner responsible for said jurisdiction shall be tasked with delegating or assuming the duties of delivering the notice of, and the execution of said warrant for the person.

Should an individual have no evidence of activity within the State of Mayflower for a period of thirty consecutive days, either in the Lee County game, or any of the official State of Mayflower Discord servers as listed in the #information channel of the State of Mayflower Discord server, they shall be deemed inactive.

Upon the Chief Medical Examiner finding evidence of an inactive person, the Medical Review Board shall meet to review the report. If the Medical Review Board, with a unanimous vote, concludes that the evidence is sufficient to take action, the board shall write a death certificate and present it to the Chief Medical Examiner.
(a) Periods of inactivity automatically expire if a person communicates in any official Mayflower Discord server, or are seen in-game.
(i) Said person must then be removed from the registry, typically without notice, and are not protected from death investigations.
(ii) A person may refile for scheduled inactivity if this occurs.
Death certificates are unenforceable until signed by the Chief Medical Examiner.

The Chief Medical Examiner is required to contact the recipient of the certificate where the recipient has a period of forty-eight (48) hours to contest the death certificate. If the recipient fails to respond within said period, the Chief Medical Examiner may formally sign the death certificate.
(a) The Chief Medical Examiner shall be required to attempt to contact the recipient via Discord direct messages.

(i) If the Chief Medical Examiner is unable to directly message the recipient, the Chief Medical Examiner shall publicly announce the death certificate in a relevant official Discord server. No other means of contacting the recipient need be exhausted.
(b) In the event the recipient wishes to contest the certificate, the Chief Medical Examiner shall be unable to sign the death certificate, unless;
(i) The Chief Medical Examiner may obtain a written signature from a Justice or the Chief Justice of the Mayflower Supreme Court to override any contest.

The State Medical Examiner’s Office shall maintain a line of communication in which both inactivity can be reported, and death certificates can be challenged in the event that the recipient has been falsely flagged. The State Medical Examiner’s Office shall be compelled to revoke death certificates if the individual challenges the certificate, provided Section V. (b) (iii), is not met.

The recipient of a death certificate; if employed in a public agency, department, judiciary, elected office, or any other official position within the State of Mayflower; shall have those positions forfeited and made vacant.
(a) If the recipient wishes to return to activity, they may not be denied the ability to be appointed, elected, or employed in public office because of the issuance of a death certificate alone.

(b) Employers shall not further prohibit the recipient from reentering employment within a public agency unless other factors listed in the Public Servants Act disqualify their entry into a department.

Any individual who willingly or knowingly employs, or keeps employed an individual within a public entity, or any likewise organization who has received a death certificate, who additionally received warning from the State Medical Examiner's Office via formal letter, shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 “Gross Misconduct."
Any employee of the State Medical Examiner's Office who willingly, knowingly, and intentionally engaged in the false issuing of a death certificate is guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 “Gross Misconduct."

Any employee of the State Medical Examiner’s Office who uses the privileges afforded to their office to discriminate against individuals based on personal grievance, or on the promise, action, or exchange of goods or services shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1303 “Gross Misconduct."
The term “Department of Justice” shall refer to:
(a) The cabinet-level agency ordained under Article VI of the State Constitution with the charge of execution of the laws of the State, and representation of the State in all matters before a Court.
The term “Attorney General” shall refer to:
(a) The constitutionally ordained cabinet-level department head of the Department of Justice who serves as Chief Attorney, Chief Prosecutor, and Chief Law Enforcement Officer of the State.
This chapter may be cited as the "Department of Justice Act."
The Attorney General shall give his advice and opinion on questions of law when required by the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, or any Cabinet Secretary.
The Attorney General shall retain oversight and authority over law enforcement agencies to ensure proper execution of duties in line with the laws of the state and the constitution.
The Attorney General may, as a result of a tip filed with their office, commission a department’s internal affairs investigations into any official of a department including their head.

The Attorney General may commission review of a department’s policies to ensure such policies are in line with the laws of the State. The Attorney General may, as a result of these reviews, issue recommendations regarding a change of policy, or a memorandum regarding a policy-shift.

The Attorney General shall conduct regular audits of departments and agencies to ensure all internal affairs complaints have been handled ethically and properly, as well as compliance with State policies and laws.

The Attorney General may review administrative actions of a department to prevent civil litigation. Such review shall only be evaluated within the full context of the law and shall not incur any subjective review unless deemed necessary.

The Attorney General, as part of their abilities to review administrative actions, may overturn any administrative action to prevent civil litigation against the State, or any municipal/county government entity on behalf of the State.
The Attorney General may refuse to defend an agent of an agency if that agency does not conform to rules or procedures promulgated by the Attorney General’s Office.

Except as otherwise authorized by law, the conduct of litigation in which the State of Mayflower, an agency, or officer thereof is a party, or is interested, and securing evidence therefor, is reserved to officers of the Department of Justice, under the direction of the Attorney General.

Except as otherwise authorized by law, the conduct of litigation in which the State of Mayflower, an agency, or officer thereof is a party, or is interested, and securing evidence therefor, is reserved to officers of the Department of Justice, under the direction of the Attorney General.

The Solicitor General, or any officer of the Department of Justice, may be sent by the Attorney General to any Court in the State of Mayflower to attend to the interests of the State of Mayflower in a suit pending in a court of the State of Mayflower, or in a court of a City or Township, or to attend to any other interest of the State of Mayflower. If one so exists, the Solicitor General shall be admitted into the Supreme Court Bar.

Except when the Attorney General in a particular case directs otherwise, the Attorney General and the Solicitor General shall conduct and argue suits and appeals in the Supreme Court in which the State of Mayflower is interested.

When the Attorney General considers it in the interests of the State of Mayflower, he may personally conduct and argue any case in a court of the State of Mayflower in which the State of Mayflower is interested, or he may direct the Solicitor General or any officer of the Department of Justice to do so.

Except as otherwise authorized by law, the Attorney General shall supervise all litigation to which the State of Mayflower, an agency, or officer thereof is a party, and shall direct all State Attorneys, Assistant Attorneys General, and Solicitors General in the conduct of litigation.

The Attorney General shall promulgate rules and regulations which require the disqualification of any officer or employee of the Department of Justice, including an Assistant Attorney General or a member of such attorney’s staff, from participation in a particular investigation or prosecution if such participation may result in a personal, financial, or political conflict of interest, or the appearance thereof. Such rules and regulations may provide that a willful violation of any provision thereof may result in removal from office.
The Attorney General shall mediate all claims to-where a government department, agency, or employee has a legal claim against another government department, agency, or employee.
(a) The findings of the Attorney General shall be res judicata and not appealable.
In civil cases against an agent of; or the government, the Attorney General or his designee shall attempt to mediate and serve as initial arbitrator.
(a) No case against an agent of; or the government shall be heard by the civil courts without there first being a decision on the mediation.
(b) If the Attorney General finds in favor of the plaintiff against the government, that decision shall be final and unappealable so long as the relief demanded is granted.
(c) If the Attorney General finds in favor of the government, or does not grant all relief demanded, then the plaintiff may proceed with a civil action in the State courts.
(d) Any statute of civil limitations for torts shall be tolled during the mediation process, starting on the date a mediation request is transmitted to the Attorney General.

The Attorney General shall create forms for public use that will allow citizens to submit tips on crime; submit tips on law enforcement misconduct; submit tips on arbitrary administrative actions; and submit tips on public corruption.
(a) The Attorney General may offer monetary incentives in exchange for the submission of a tip.
The Attorney General may administer oaths, examine witnesses, take depositions, and receive evidence.
The Attorney General may issue subpoenas, and; order the taking of depositions and order responses to written interrogations.

The Attorney General may through motion vacate an arrest, citation or other form of detention on the basis that there exists insufficient probable cause for such arrest, citation or detention. No court shall review the contents of the vacature order nor deny for any reason except insofar as to determine if the motion is in proper form and certified by the Attorney General. The order of vacature by Court shall be res judicata.

The Attorney General has the ability to refuse to defend a government official in suits of official misconduct - if that Attorney General follows up the case with a criminal investigation against the individual, as well as provide injunctive relief in the form of an order that repairs the injury caused.

Whenever any person, sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, cooperative, joint venture, freelance, non-profit, or other commercial business entity, registered or unregistered, engages in repeated fraudulent or illegal acts, or otherwise demonstrates persistent fraud or illegality in the carrying on, conducting, or transaction of business, whether it be public, or other private business, the Attorney General may apply to the Mayflower District Court for an order enjoining the continuance of such business activity or any fraudulent or illegal acts, directing restitution and damages. The court may award the relief applied for or so much thereof as it may deem proper. The word "fraud" or "fraudulent" as used herein shall include any device, scheme, or artifice to defraud, and any deception, misrepresentation, concealment, suppression, false pretense, false promise, or unconscionable contractual provisions. The term "persistent fraud" or "illegality" as used herein shall include the continuance or carrying on of any fraudulent or illegal act or conduct. The term "repeated" as used herein shall include the repetition of any separate and distinct fraudulent or illegal act, or conduct that affects more than one person.

In connection with any such application, the Attorney General is authorized to take proof, make a determination of the relevant facts, issue subpoenas, and administer oaths. If a person subpoenaed to attend upon such inquiry fails to obey the command of a subpoena without reasonable cause, or if a person in attendance upon such inquiry shall, without reasonable cause, refuse to be sworn or to be examined or to answer a question or to produce a book or paper, when ordered so to do by the officer conducting such inquiry, he shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1503. The Attorney General or their designated officer in the Department of Justice is authorized to prosecute any person for perjury committed during the course of any investigation conducted pursuant to this section.

In any case where the Attorney General has the authority to initiate a civil action or proceeding to enforce a law of this state, the Attorney General may, in lieu of such action, accept an assurance of discontinuance from any person engaged in or who has engaged in the act or practice violating that law. This assurance may include a stipulation for the voluntary payment by the alleged violator of the reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the Attorney General during the investigation. Evidence of a violation of this assurance shall serve as prima facie proof of a violation of the applicable law in any subsequent civil action or proceeding initiated by the Attorney General.

The Attorney General may delegate the authority designated to them by 3 M.S.C. 1 §§ 7219, 7220, 7221, 7222, 7223, 7224, and 7225 to an inferior officer or other employee within the Department of Justice.

An investigative agency shall be defined as any agency that: Investigates complaints of misconduct against its own agents; Investigates complaints of criminal activity in general; Investigates complaints of criminal activity against its own agents. To ensure a proper case and court pipeline, the Attorney General shall have general oversight abilities over such investigative agencies.
The Attorney General may promulgate rules for investigations and ethics.

The Attorney General may sanction investigative agencies that fail to follow rules and procedure by revoking that agency’s ability to petition the courts for warrants, submit cases to be prosecuted, or other tools provided by law that investigative agencies get to enjoy.
Any good standing investigative agency shall, upon the finding of any criminal action, refer the case files to the Attorney General for prosecution.
The Attorney General shall retain oversight over all investigative agencies, and their caseflow.

The Attorney General may issue memorandums to investigative agencies or departments directing the agency to investigate and submit cases as part of the prosecutorial doctrine of the Attorney General’s Office.

The Attorney General may define the means and ways it wishes to prosecute certain crimes. The Attorney General may also establish priorities in which he wishes to prosecute some crimes more than others by realm of their importance to the general welfare of the people.

The Attorney General may choose to, if he has adequate constitutional backing, declare provisions of a law “unenforceable” by transmitting in writing the reasons for such declaration to the Governor and presiding officer of the State Senate.
The Attorney General may choose to, if evaluated so in his priorities, not prosecute specific crimes due to the crime not having priority over other prosecutions the state is bringing.

The Attorney General shall have the ability to appoint a special counsel to investigate any State Senator, department head, an individual running for election, or other government officials at the State, County, or Municipal levels.
(a) The Attorney General shall not appoint a special counsel to investigate a private citizen.
The Attorney General shall provide the jurisdiction in which the special counsel may operate in.
The Special Counsel, while within his jurisdiction, shall have the authority and ability to exercise investigative and prosecutorial functions as the Attorney General.

The Special Counsel shall determine whether and to what extent to inform or consult the Attorney General about the conduct of their responsibilities pursuant to the guidelines set by the Attorney General in the appointment order.
The Special Counsel shall comply with all rules and procedures of the Attorney General’s Office.
The Special Counsel shall not be subject to any day-to-day supervision by a member of the Attorney General’s Office.

The Special Counsel and staff shall be subject to disciplinary action for misconduct and breach of ethical duties under the same standards and to the same extent as are other employees of the Attorney General’s Office.

A Special Counsel may request the assignment of appropriate Attorney General’s Office employees to assist the Special Counsel. The Attorney General’s Office shall gather and provide the Special Counsel with the names and resumes of appropriate personnel available for detail.
The Special Counsel may also request the details of specific employees, and the office for which the designated employee works shall make reasonable efforts to accommodate the request.

The Special Counsel shall assign the duties and supervise the work of such employees while they are assigned to the Special Counsel. If necessary, the Special Counsel may request that additional personnel be hired or assigned from outside the Attorney General’s Office.
All personnel in the Attorney General’s Office shall cooperate to the fullest extent possible with the Special Counsel.
The Special Counsel may hire special investigators as he sees fit to investigate a claim under his jurisdiction.

The Department of Justice shall incorporate an investigation bureau (hereinafter “Mayflower Bureau of Investigation” or “MBI”); which shall be the primary investigative agency utilized by the Department of Justice, and shall have state-wide authority within the State of Mayflower.

records.text: When a Municipal Department Head’s Office becomes vacant, in the absence of a Functional Municipal Government, the County Executive shall nominate their replacement. This replacement must be vetted and ratified by a ⅔ majority vote by that County’s Board or legislature.

When a Municipal Department Head’s Office becomes vacant, in the absence of a Functional Municipal Government and a Functional County Government within the same area, the Governor of the State of Mayflower shall nominate their replacement. This replacement must be vetted and ratified by a ⅔ majority vote of the Mayflower State Senate.
Should the vote fail, a new nomination should be made.
All government officials serve at the pleasure of the people, elected officials who serve the people may remove municipal department heads as defined herein.
The County Executive, in absence of a Functional Municipal Government, may remove a Municipal Department Head.
The County Board by ¾ vote during a session of the county legislature may remove a Municipal Department Head in absence of a Functional Municipal Government.
The State Governor, in absence of a Functional Municipal Government and Functional County Government within the same area, may remove a Municipal Department Head.

The State Senate by ¾ vote during a session of the state legislature may remove a Municipal Department Head in absence of a Functioning Municipal Government and Functioning County Government within the same area.

There shall exist under the exexutive branch a Department of Motor Vehicles, which shall be administered by a Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, who shall be appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Department of Motor Vehicles shall, under the direction of the Commissioner, retain authority over issuing, suspending, revoking, and administering all drivers license, learners permits, and vehicle registrations.
The Commissioner may hire administrative staff to fulfill the mandate of the Department.
The terms “Agency for International Intelligence” and “International Intelligence Agency” shall refer to the same body and may be used interchangeably.

The Governor may grant exceptions to Title 3, Subtitle 1, Chapter XI of the Mayflower State Code as it pertains to the Agency for International Intelligence and foreign intelligence activity. Such exceptions will be documented and in writing, but not necessarily entered into the official record if such documentation would be pernicious to state security interests.

The Agency for International Intelligence shall exist as a hybrid state security organization possessing both military and civilian attributes, operating under civilian control while supporting military operations.

context.subtitle: SUBTITLE 1:

context.subchapter: SUBCHAPTER II. THE AGENCY FOR INTERNATIONAL INTELLIGENCE

records.text: There shall be a Director of the Agency for International Intelligence, appointed by the Governor, with the advice and consent of the State Senate.
The Director of the Agency for International Intelligence shall be the Department Head of the Agency for International Intelligence.
The Director shall sit on the State Security Council and Cabinet at the discretion of the Governor.
The Director shall hold authority to classify information as “O” Classification, and to access such information as defined under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(d).
The Director may be either a civilian or commissioned military officer.

(a) If a military officer, the Director shall wear such rank and exercise the privileges, authority, and precedence appertaining thereto as directed by the Adjutant General while so serving, but shall not thereby exercise command authority over forces of the armed services except as otherwise provided by law or regulation.

The Adjutant General may, with concurrence of the Director, detail military commissioned and noncommissioned officers for service in the Agency, in which case such detailed personnel shall continue to be bound by all expectations and standards of the National Guard while reporting to appropriate military and Agency superiors.
With the consent of the Adjutant General, the Director may dispatch civilian employees of the Agency to receive initial military training in order to transfer into status under § 10306.
The Director of the International Intelligence Agency is authorized to—
(a) collect intelligence through human sources and by other appropriate means outside the State of Mayflower;

(b) provide overall direction for and coordination of the collection of national intelligence outside the State of Mayflower through human sources by elements of the intelligence community authorized to undertake such collection;
(c) correlate and evaluate intelligence related to state security;

(d) provide appropriate dissemination of such intelligence to authorized recipients, including the Governor, heads of departments and agencies of the executive branch, the Adjutant General, military generals, and the State Senate and the committees thereof;

(e) collect (including through clandestine means), process, analyze, produce, and disseminate signals intelligence information and data for foreign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes to support national and departmental missions;
(f) establish priorities for signals intelligence activities carried out by elements of the intelligence community;
(g) conduct electronic surveillance, physical searches, and other acquisitions for foreign intelligence purposes, subject to court orders where required;
(h) conduct counterintelligence activities in support of signals intelligence operations;
(i) conduct counterintelligence activities outside the State of Mayflower and coordinate counterintelligence activities conducted outside the State of Mayflower by other agencies;
(j) support military operations and other national security efforts through the provision of signals intelligence;
(k) coordinate with other elements of the intelligence community on signals intelligence matters;

(l) protect the security of Agency installations, activities, information, property, and employees by appropriate means, including such investigations of applicants, employees, contractors, and other persons with similar associations with the Agency as are necessary;

(m) terminate the employment of any officer or employee of the Agency for International Intelligence whenever the Director deems the termination of employment of such officer or employee necessary or advisable in the interests of the State of Mayflower; and
(n) perform such other functions and duties related to intelligence affecting the national security as the Governor may direct.

(o) Subject to the approval of the Governor and consistent with applicable law, the Director of the Agency for International Intelligence is authorized to conduct special activities, including covert actions intended to influence political, economic, or military conditions abroad, where it is intended that the role of the State of Mayflower will not be apparent or acknowledged publicly, except that no such activity may be conducted for the purpose of influencing domestic Mayflower political processes, public opinion, policies, or media.
The Director shall organize the Agency for International Intelligence at his discretion in a manner conducive to the mission of the Agency.
The Director shall, at least quarterly, brief and report to the State Security Council regarding the activities of the Agency for International Intelligence in such quarterly period.
The Director may–
(a) Liaise directly with federal intelligence, law enforcement, military, and diplomatic entities without intermediary approval.
(b) Determine, in consultation with the Attorney General, the legality of intelligence activities conducted under this statute.
(c) Classify, declassify, and control the dissemination of information produced or held by the Service.
(d) Grant temporary clearances for no more than 7 days to employees of the Agency for International Intelligence for information and intelligence used by the Service.
To provide compensation for assets, informants, non-public employees, and asylum seekers to advance the foreign interests of the State, the Director may–
(a) In concert and with the approval of the Director of the Law Enforcement Training Institute, provide for expedited or direct entry into a Law Enforcement Training Institute Class;
(b) In concert and with the approval of the Mayflower State Bar, provide for a transfer of equivalent certification into the State of Mayflower;
(c) In concert and with the approval of a Department Head, provide for expedited or direct entry into a public service department; and
(d) In concert and with the approval of a Department Head, provide for a promotion, transfer, or reassignment.
There shall be established an Office of State Intelligence.

records.text: All employees, regardless of employment status, shall have the following rights:

(a) Members participating in an official training exercise or Live Fire Exercise shall be afforded the right to withdraw from the exercise before the exercise begins and may do so without any consequences or action taken against them by their employer.

Law enforcement agencies and the National Guard must take reasonable measures to protect those not directly participating in any official training exercise or Live Fire Exercise. This shall include, where possible, an in-game notification notifying that an exercise is taking place.

Members of law enforcement agencies and the National Guard, who are directly involved in a Live Fire Exercise, shall be protected from civil and criminal prosecution if injuring a person/persons not directly involved in the exercise if:
(a) said person willingly endangers themselves or others; or
(b) reasonable measures have been taken to ensure the safety of those not participating in the exercise.

During a Live Fire Exercise, it shall be lawful to shoot, injure, and kill those directly involved in the exercise, provided there is mutual consent on both sides, proper permissions have been obtained, and the exercise is held in compliance with this act.

During a Live Fire Exercise, it shall be lawful to damage and destroy property belonging to the agency(s) involved in the exercise or belonging to the State, provided there is mutual consent on both sides, proper permission has been obtained, and the exercise is held in compliance with this act.
During a Live Fire Exercise, individuals directly participating shall not be held liable for any violations of the Mayflower Vehicle Code.
The host of a Live Fire Exercise shall be required to use “STARTEX” and “ENDEX” to indicate the beginning and end of an exercise.
(a) “STARTEX” and “ENDEX” must be called over the radio in the frequency(s) in which all participants of the live fire have access to.
(b) Those hosting a Live Fire Exercise are required to state STARTEX at the beginning of the exercise, else the immunities granted in this act shall be nullified.
(c) Members directly involved in the Live Fire Exercise shall be granted, by the hosting member, the right to withdraw from the exercise if needed before STARTEX is stated.

A Live Fire Exercise may not last more than make it four (4) hours after STARTEX is declared. After this point all immunities granted in this act shall be nullified for all members involved in the exercise.

Any person who states STARTEX, or states that a Live Fire Exercise is in effect, without being in compliance with the regulations set forth by this act for hosting a Live Fire Exercise and proceeds to commit any civil or criminal offenses shall be held liable for the commission of said offenses.

Live Fire Exercises hosted by the Mayflower National Guard solely on National Guard property/installations shall only require the written permission of a senior officer within the National Guard, at the rank of Major or above.
(a) These Live Fires only require ten (10) minutes advance public notice.

records.text: The Governor and Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation shall each have the authority to designate an organization, association, group of individuals, or individual, whether formal or informal, as a Terrorist Organization, with the advice and consent of the Attorney General, if:
(a) the Terrorist Organization conducts terrorist activity, or attempts to commit or commits the act of Treason, supported with articulable evidence; or
(b) it is an organization, association, or group of two or more individuals which acts in conjunction with a Terrorist Organization, supported with articulable evidence; and
(c) it poses a direct threat to the safety and security of the State, supported with articulable evidence; or
(d) it poses a direct threat to the interests of the State, supported with articulable evidence.

The Governor and Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation shall each have the authority to designate an organization, association, group of individuals, or individual, whether formal or informal, as a Terrorist Organization, with the advice and consent of the Secretary of State, if:
(a) the State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization conducts terrorist activity, or attempts to commit or commits the act of Insurrection, supported with articulable evidence; or

(b) it is an organization, association, or group of two or more individuals which acts in conjunction with a State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, supported with articulable evidence, supported with articulable evidence; and
(c) it is sponsored by a foreign government, supported with articulable evidence; and
(d) it poses a direct threat to the safety and security of the State, supported with articulable evidence; or
(e) it poses a direct threat to the interests of the State, supported with articulable evidence.
The Secretary of State shall maintain a database of all Terrorist Organizations and State-Sponsored Terrorist Organizations.
For the purposes of this act, the term ‘terrorist activity’ shall be defined as:
(a) The act of committing Criminal Anarchy.
(b) The act of detonating an explosive at an official state event.
(c) The act of being in unlawful possession of a self-propelled explosive.
(d) The pattern of coordinated mass violence over a period of 72 hours.
It shall be prohibited to employ any person who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization.

(a) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may temporarily commandeer vehicles owned by the target of the covert search for the purpose of this provision.

(b) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may delay notifying the target of the covert search, and providing the search receipt, for up to 14 days after the execution of the covert search, as decided by the judge who authorized the covert search warrant.
(c) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation must notify the Senate Standing Committee on Military & Intelligence Affairs prior to its execution.
(d) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may not be authorized to seize any items, regardless of its legality, except for firearms and explosives.
(e) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may temporarily detain the target of the covert search in order to execute such a search.

Every month, the designated Senate Standing Committee shall review the implementation of this Act to ensure that there is no abuse of power. If there is no such Senate Standing Committee, the Senate as a whole shall be responsible for the review of the implementation of this act.

records.text: Any person who participates in or incites an armed rebellion or violent resistance against the government or laws of the state shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1106 Insurrection.
Any person who participates in a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 5103 Engagement in a Terrorist Organization.

Any person who directs or organizes a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 5104 Direction of a Terrorist Organization.

Any person who gives material or financial support to a Terrorist Organization or a State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, or violates Section VI of this act, shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 5105 Supporting a Terrorist Organization.

If two or more members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization are conducting crime together, or aiding each other to do crime, they shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 5103 Engagement in a Terrorist Organization.

Any person who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization and is in possession of a firearm shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 6102 Unlicensed possession of a firearm.

Any person who loiters with two or more other individuals who are a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, while also being a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization themself, if the purpose or effect of that behavior is to enable a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to establish control over identifiable areas, to intimidate others from entering those areas, or to conceal illegal activities, and who ignores an order to disperse from a peace officer, shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 4105 Unlawful assembly.

Any person who utilizes advertisement boards in order to display how to join, or how to participate in, a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 5103 Engagement in a Terrorist Organization.

Any individual who, owing allegiance to a foreign nation state, participates in acts of war against the State shall be liable for conviction and arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1107 Participation of War as a Foreign Actor.
The Governor shall have the power to temporarily deport the following officials of a Foreign Nation-State during a state of war that has been declared on them:
(a) State Governor and Lieutenant Governor, or its equivalents.
(b) Secretary of State, or its equivalent.
(c) Members of their State Legislature, or its equivalents.
(d) Head and deputy head of their military body.
(e) Head and deputy head of their intelligence body.
No individual shall be deported unless they:
(a) Have been convicted of a crime under Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter I of the Mayflower Criminal Code.
(b) Are a member of a military or intelligence organization of a Nation-State which Mayflower is at war with.
(c) Are sentenced to death.
This section shall not be construed to inhibit the power of any other act, law, or provision which permits deportations for any reason not prohibited by law.
The term “Presiding Officer” shall refer to:
(a) The President of the Senate or, in the absence of the President, the President pro tempore to a convened session of the Senate at-large; and
(b) The chair of a Standing Senate Committee or any member designated by the chair to preside in the chair’s absence to a convened meeting of a Standing Senate Committee.
The term “convened Senate or Senate Committee” shall refer to:
(a) A session of the Senate at-large, who are present and roll called to be in session; or
(b) A hearing, session, or meeting of any Standing Senate Committee who are present and roll called to be in session and convened.
The term “Sergeant-at-Arms” shall refer to:

(a) Any state-certified peace officer who is currently employed in a law enforcement agency, who is in good standing with the agency, and who is appointed by the President of the Senate to head the Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms, or the deputies under the Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms appointed by the Sergeant-at-Arms.
The term “gallery” shall refer to:
(a) Any area within the Senate chamber or committee room designated for public observation of proceedings.
The term “classified information” shall refer to:
(a) Any information to be means any information that is classified as:
(i) "Top Secret" under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a);
(ii) "Secret" under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(b); or
(iii) "Confidential" under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(c).
A convened Senate or Senate Committee may, by resolution—
(a) Hold an individual in violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1502, "Contempt of Senate," if the individual:
(i) Does not comply with a subpoena, writ, or order issued by a convened Senate or Senate Committee; or
(ii) Willfully obstructs a convened Senate or Senate Committee while it conducts an investigation, inquiry, or legislative action.
(b) And decide on a reasonable punishment as dictated by the Mayflower Criminal Code.
Should a resolution pass, the Sergeant-at-Arms of the Mayflower Legislature shall be responsible for the serving of the resolution.
The Presiding Officer of a convened Senate or Senate Committee, without a resolution, may direct the Sergeant-at-arms to—
(a) Remove any individual from the chamber, committee room, gallery, or any area under Senate control, if the individual:

(i) Disrupts a convened Senate or Senate Committee or its functions; acts disorderly therein; or, after having been removed previously therefrom by the Sergeant-at-Arms returns to the chamber or committee room during that same convened session.
(ii) A sudden disruptive demonstration occurs in the gallery, to which only the participating demonstrators may be cleared from the floor.
(b) Hold an individual in violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1502, "Contempt of Senate or 1 M.S.C. § 1506, "Disorderly Conduct before the Senate” if the individual:
(i) Commits the acts listed in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a)(i)
(ii) Commits the acts listed in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a)(ii)
(c) Clear the gallery of a convened Senate or Senate Committee and seal it if:
(i) A sudden reveal of classified information has occurred in a convened Senate or Senate Committee to which the public are present.
(ii) Commits the acts listed in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a)(ii)
(d) Hold an individual in violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1318, "Obstruction of Senate", if the individual commits the acts defined in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1303.

Any individual(s) removed or held in contempt under this subchapter may file a written appeal to the Standing Senate Committee on Ethics within forty-eight (48) hours; the appeal shall not stay the removal, citation, or arrest unless the committee votes in a two-thirds majority to stay it pending review.

Any person who knowingly and willfully; influences, obstructs, or impedes, or endeavors to influence, obstruct, or impede, the due exercise of the Senate's powers, including any inquiry, investigation, or proceeding; corruptly alters, destroys, mutilates, or conceals any document, record, or evidence with intent to impair its integrity or availability for use in a Senate proceeding; fails to comply with a lawful subpoena, order, or writ issued by the Senate; obstructs, hinders, or impedes the Sergeant-at-arms in the course of their duties as instructed by the Presiding Officer, or by resolution; intimidates, threatens, or corruptly persuades another person, or attempts to do so, with intent to influence, delay, or prevent testimony or the production of evidence in a Senate proceeding; or provided false, misleading, or incomplete information to the Senate with intent to deceive or obstruct shall be guilty of "Obstruction of Senate"

The State Legislature may, by resolution, refer to the Committee on State Security to initiate an investigation into any activities of the National Guard that the State Legislature determines may exceed statutory authority, pose risks to public safety, or warrant legislative review due to suspected irregularities or concerns.
(a) Such investigations may include, but are not limited to:
(i) Review of deployment records, operational reports, and incident summaries.
(ii) Subpoena of witnesses, documents, or other evidence related to Guard activities.
(iii) Hearings on matters involving potential civilian impacts, operational overreach, or compliance with state law.

The Governor, the Adjutant General of the National Guard, and other relevant military officials shall cooperate fully with any such investigation, providing timely access to information unless prohibited by state law or state security classifications.
“Commission” means the State Archive Commission created under this Act.
“State Archivist” means the chief executive officer of the Commission.
“Archive” means any record, document, file, communication, digital item, or preserved material under the custody of the Commission.
“Restricted Archive” means any record designated as restricted by the State Archivist pursuant to this Act. A restricted archive is one which can not be publicly accessible.
“Reasonable period of time” means a timeframe determined by the State Archivist and communicated in writing to the person or office required to submit materials.
There shall be an established independent government agency known as the “State Archive Commission”.
The “State Archive Commission” shall only report to the Senate Committee on Ethics when formally requested.

The commission shall be directed by the “State Archivist" who shall be recommended by the governor, with the advice and consent of the Mayflower State Senate. The “State Archivist" holds the authority to manage operations, archiving and all affairs of the commission
The State Archivist may appoint employees and administrative officers as necessary for the operation of the Commission and shall supervise their performance.
If any required office or position becomes vacant, the State Archivist shall assume the responsibilities of that office until it is filled.
The State Archivist shall appoint the following officers to assist in fulfilling Commission duties:
(a) Assistant State Archivist for the Executive Branch;
(b) Assistant State Archivist for the Legilsative Branch;
(c) Assistant State Archivist for the Judiciary Branch;
It shall be the responsibility of the State Archivist to maintain a platform where all archives can be placed.
The State Archivist may classify any archive or item as “Restricted” if:
(a) Its disclosure poses a threat to the national or governmental security of the State;
(b) The item is under investigation for fraud, falsification, or suspected unreliability;
(c) The information is strictly private and such determination is made by the State Archivist; or
(d) The Governor or Attorney General submits a written request stating justification, and the State Archivist approves such justification.

There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of business completed by the legislative under each congress. This includes; bills, members, record of senate officers, and all other information authorised by the State Archivist.
(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require a member of the senate, or a senate officer to submit all required materials to the state archive.
(b) Any member of the senate, or a senate officer may submit a request to the State Archivist to send, or archive requested materials.
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of all pardons, reprieves and commutations.
(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of medals or commendations awarded by the Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State, and the Order of Mayflower.
(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

(b) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require any government official or citizen, to submit all required materials to the state archive which is in regards to medals or commendations awarded.

There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of business completed by the Supreme Court and District Court. This includes; opinions and rulings, orders and judgments, court administrative records or other information authorised by the State Archivist.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the Chief Judge of the District, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

This includes; all oaths of office for elected officers or officers appointed by the Governor, and all other information authorised by the State Archivist.
(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.
(b) It lays the responsibility of the governor, or a delegate to inform and submit all required information to the State Archive Commission within a reasonable period of time.

The State Archivist may authorise the establishment of further archived materials or items. The State Archivist, requires any citizen, or government official (or a delegate) to submit required information requested by the State Archive Commission.
The "Guard" shall be known as the Mayflower National Guard, or any known variation thereof.
