In this subtitle, a Military Installation means any of the following properties below:
(a) Fort Standish within the Military Exclusion Zone;
(b) Lander City Berginson Armory;
(c) Winchester Recruitment Center; and
(d) Camp Bryant.

In this subtitle, the "Military Exclusion Zone" or "MEZ" shall be defined as the land surrounding the Fort Standish and Camp Bryant properties within the perimeter formed by appropriate signage and/or perimeter fencing.
(a) This shall extend to any river or stream directly below a perimeter fence or posted sign and open water within 1000 studs of any perimeter fence or posted sign.

Unauthorized individual” shall refer to any individual who enters a Military Exclusion Zone while not explicitly authorized by an on-duty Senior Officer, or Military Police Officer to enter that Military Exclusion Zone.
“Drawn firearm” shall refer to any firearm that is being held using at least one hand and is not contained wholly within a storage device.
A “Military Arrest Order (‘MAO’)” shall be defined as:
(a) Any issued order, by a sitting Judge within the State of Mayflower, to have a person arrested for a specific charge that falls under military jurisdiction.
A “Military Seizure Order (‘MSO’)” shall be defined as:

(a) Any issued order, by a sitting Judge within the State of Mayflower, to have a person and/or their property inspected for any military property to be seized, or any other articles that fall under military jurisdiction.
The term “Military Housing” or “Military Home” shall refer to:
(a) “Any Residential Property within a Military Exclusion Zone, as defined within Title 3, Chapter VII of the Mayflower State Code.”
The term Forward Operating Base or FOB shall be defined as the public land temporarily utilized by the National Guard as a military base.
Militia shall refer to an organisation of civilians who wish to exercise their 2nd Amendment rights in a regulated manner.
A General Officer shall refer to an individual holding the rank of Brigadier General or higher, excluding the Commander-in-Chief.

Honor Guard shall refer to the ceremonial unit established and maintained by the Mayflower National Guard pursuant to 3 M.S.C. 4 § 8101, tasked with rendering honors at official events and state functions, safeguarding designated sites, and upholding ceremonial drill proficiency.
Parade Fire shall refer to ceremonial volleys or salutes conducted by the Honor Guard during authorized events.

Designated Sites shall refer to the State Capitol, Supreme Court, The Volunteers’ Valor Memorial, and any other locations approved for ceremonial activity by the Governor, Adjutant General or their designee.
(a) Volunteers’ Valor Memorial shall refer to the memorial site located in Winchester, dedicated to the service and sacrifice of the 67th Eirinnite Regiment.
Proctees shall refer to individuals designated by the Adjutant General for ceremonial escort or protection during official Honor Guard operations.
The detainment powers established herein shall override those otherwise stipulated within the Mayflower State Code, including those established by the Chapter on Police Detainment Limitations.

(a) This scope of detainment powers within this section does not apply to the powers of detention or arrest delegated to Military Police, who shall retain those powers and will not be bound by the provisions of this section while serving in their capacity as Military Police.

The Adjutant General of the Mayflower National Guard is delegated the power to equip with, provide training in the use of, and dictate policies governing the use of handcuffs by guardsmen. The Adjutant General shall be empowered to instruct guardsmen, through the use of policy or direct orders, to detain any citizen in breach of state law within the direct vicinity of any Military Installation provided such detention is necessary to prevent damage to any person, property, or to prevent any action deemed subversive to the continuity of government.

During Martial Law, the Adjutant General shall have the power to dictate policy related to the detention of individuals who pose a threat to the restoration of order within the state. Any such detention should be ended as soon as is practical after the detaining guardsman becomes aware, or could reasonably be considered to have been made aware, of the end of any Martial Law.

A guardsmen shall not arrest any person, unless the guardsman is a serving member of the military police. Guardsmen shall transfer custody of any detainee to a member of the military police or civilian law enforcement as soon as it is practical to do so.
(a) Guardsmen, or any individual processing the arrest of the detainee, can not detain any individual for more than 20 minutes, at which point they must be released.
(b) If the detainee, on their own accord, takes measures to voluntarily delay the arrest process, the time taken during the delay shall not be counted to the overall time they have been detained for.

The Adjutant General may dictate policies allowing Guardsmen to transport an individual under military detention in such cases where transport is necessary to bring the individual to an officer able to make an arrest. Such situations include, but are not limited to, the transport of an individual to a point within city limits, in order to allow a peace officer with confined jurisdiction to affect the arrest of the individual.

records.text: It shall be unlawful for any individual to possess an Explosive Device, except serving members of the National Guard as stipulated by this section.
The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to authorize, and delegate the authorization process, for access to and use of Explosive Devices amongst guardsmen.
Those authorized to possess said Explosive Devices must only utilize them under at least one of the following parameters:
(a) The designee is participating in sanctioned training conducted with the knowledge and written permission of a Senior Officer.
(b) The designee is participating in an activation of the Guard, related to a declaration of war or an ongoing war.
(c) The designee is participating in an deployment of the Guard, related to counter terrorism or counter insurgency operations.
(d) The designee is detonating an Explosive Device seized by the Mayflower National Guard or law enforcement agencies in order to conduct an explosive ordnance disposal.

Any utilization of an Explosive Device that causes intentional and/or negligent damage or non-combatant casualties shall be properly reported, documented, and sent to the Adjutant General or his designee to allow for review by the Senate’s Intelligence & Military Affairs Committee, the Legislature at large, or a court of law.
Guardsmen may take pistols, as defined in 4 M.S.C. 5 § 2201, off-duty in accordance with rules and regulations set by the Adjutant General.

(a) This subchapter only applies when the pistol is physically present on the person, and does not extend to:
(i) A vehicle;
(ii) A dwelling; or
(iii) Any other method of storage where the pistol would not be present on the person.
(b) This subchapter does not exempt any person from any requirements or responsibilities normally required when carrying a firearm.

Any guardsmen who carries a pistol off-duty under this subchapter is required to identify themselves to any peace officer upon request, in addition to stating that they are employed with the Mayflower National Guard.
Members of the Mayflower National Guard shall be free from civil and criminal liability for violations of the Mayflower Vehicle Code when—

It shall be unlawful for any individual to manufacture/create or attempt to manufacture/create an Explosive Device, except serving members of the National Guard or a registered business authorized by the Adjutant General through written consent as stipulated within this section.
The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to authorize, and delegate the authorization process, for access and to use of materials necessary to manufacture/create an Explosive Device.

The Adjutant General shall retain the express authority to enter into contracts with registered businesses to manufacture/create Explosive Devices for use by the National Guard and armed forces within the State.

A registered business manufacturing/creating Explosive Devices shall be authorized to possess any paraphernalia that would otherwise be considered illegal contraband provided that the intended use of the material is to fulfil functions necessary to furnish the National Guard or armed forces with Explosive Devices.

A registered business manufacturing/creating Explosive Devices shall be authorized to possess Explosive Devices that would otherwise be considered illegal contraband provided that the intended use of the material is to fulfil functions necessary to furnish the National Guard or armed forces with Explosive Devices.

The Mayflower National Guard shall establish and maintain a body known as the Military Police. This body shall be subordinate and answerable to Command Group, or any administrative entity supervising the body, who shall appoint a Senior Officer, hereinafter referred to as “Commanding Officer”, to oversee and direct the Military Police.
The Military Police shall be the military law enforcement branch of the Mayflower National Guard.
(a) The Military Police shall be tasked with enforcing Guard regulations, protecting Military Installations, convoys and members of the Guard.
“Military Police” shall be defined as military law enforcement officers.
“Military Police Officers” shall be defined as Commissioned Officers within the Military Police.
Members of the National Guard must meet the following prerequisites before joining any Military Police unit or body:
(a) The guardsman holds an active Law Enforcement Training Institute certification.
(b) The individual is currently serving within the Mayflower National Guard.
The Military Police shall have a budget given to the Commanding Officer by the Adjutant General and his Deputy.
This subchapter shall not apply during peacetime, outside of an activation of the Guard by the Governor as prescribed by the Constitution.
The Military Police shall operate in any place where the Mayflower National Guard are operating from or based, including locality surrounding serving members of the Guard.
(a) This shall not be limited to overseas.

Military Police shall be given temporary jurisdiction within the state in which their service and assistance has been requested by any peace officer of the state. This shall include, but not limited to, “10-58” or “58” calls on a radio or when Military Police assistance is specifically requested.
Military Police may not assume custody of a person from civilian peace officers unless:
(a) The person is a serving member of the Guard.
(b) The person has a Military Seizure Order or Military Arrest Order issued by the District Court.

(i) Members of civilian law enforcement that fail to turn over a suspect with an active Search Warrant relating to military property or equipment, MSO or MAO shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Justice” and “Misconduct” as defined within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

The Military Police have jurisdiction to conduct traffic stops when attempting to detain, or when otherwise authorized to arrest, on-duty national guardsmen when a crime, Defense Policy violation or a Code of Conduct violation has occurred. Military Police may also conduct traffic stops on sections of roadways within, or adjacent to, a Military Exclusion Zone.
The Military Police may only have jurisdiction to engage in a vehicle pursuit to detain or arrest a person if:
(a) A felony has been committed against on-duty national guardsmen and said person is evading Military Police.
(b) A person has been issued a Search Warrant relating to military property or equipment, a Military Seizure Order or Military Arrest Order by the courts and is evading Military Police.
(c) A crime or Defense Policy violation was committed by an on-duty guardsmen and said guardsmen are evading Military Police.
(d) A vehicle pursuit is initiated in or passes through a MEZ.

The Military Police shall have the power to freely search any Military Home, as defined in Title 4, Subtitle I of the Mayflower State Code, in accordance to regulations set by the Adjutant General or his designee.
Military Police may only have jurisdiction stipulated in this if they are clearly identifiable as a member of the Military Police.

The Military Police shall hold the exclusive jurisdiction to serve and execute Search Warrants relating to or involving military equipment/property, Military Seizure Orders and Military Arrest Orders issued by the District Court.

records.text: An “authorized guardsmen” or any variation thereof means a guardsmen who is a legitimate member of the Mayflower National Guard, through proper documentation such as a United Columbian Armed Forces Service Identification Card (U.C. Army ID).
In this section, “Mayflower Army National Guard” means the Mayflower National Guard as recited in earlier sections of this subtitle, as amended.
It is hereby authorized for the Judge Advocate General’s Corps of the Mayflower Army National Guard to engage in all legal activities under state law.

The Judge Advocate General’s Corps of the Mayflower Army National Guard is a staff corps and component of the headquarters of the Mayflower Army National Guard. It shall be organized in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Adjutant General of the Mayflower Army National Guard while it is a state agent, carrying out any obligation and function to the state while in peacetime and unactivated by the federal government.

There is in the headquarters component of the Mayflower Army National Guard a Staff Judge Advocate for the Mayflower Army National Guard. The Staff Judge Advocate shall be appointed directly by the Adjutant General, and serve at his command and pleasure.
The Staff Judge Advocate, under the direction of the Adjutant General, shall:
(a) Perform duties relating to legal matters arising in the Mayflower Army National Guard as may be assigned to him or her;
(b) Establish minimum requirements for prospective candidates to become judge advocates, including pay grade and benefits, with the consent of the Adjutant General;
(c) Either oversee or appoint in his name an officer or officers to oversee the various functions, as given by the Adjutant General, of the Judge Advocate General’s Corps; and
(d) Perform such other duties as may be assigned to him.

There is in the headquarters component of the Mayflower Army National Guard a Deputy Staff Judge Advocate for the Mayflower Army National Guard. The Deputy Staff Judge Advocate shall be appointed by the Adjutant General, with the advice of the Staff Judge Advocate, and serve at the command and pleasure of the Adjutant General.

The Deputy Staff Judge Advocate shall perform any of the duties of the Staff Judge Advocate either in his absence, delegated by the Staff Judge Advocate or under the direction of the Adjutant General from time to time.
All references to “prosecutor” herein shall refer to a judge advocate who is designated a prosecutor with the Judge Advocate General’s Corps unless stated otherwise.

records.text: All Militias are required to be registered with the Office of the Adjutant General.

Additional requirements may be set and published by the Adjutant General or his designee in a publicly accessible space.

Individuals who have received an honorable discharge from the Mayflower National Guard must be given priority membership status, provided they qualify as eligible members.
The Adjutant General, or his designee are to establish requirements that Militias are to follow to continue active operation.
Militias are to maintain their own publicly available operations policy, as well as maintaining a public database of all qualified members.
(a) Citizens who have four in total or more active misdemeanor records or have an active felony record are not eligible to be qualified for membership.

Militias may be deployed alongside the Mayflower National Guard at the request of the Governor, Adjutant General or his designee, Militias will be subservient to all regulations set forth to the Mayflower National Guard and all members, regardless of their internal Militia rank, will be obligated to follow orders given by a Senior Officer, ranked Major or above, within the Mayflower National Guard.

The Mayflower National Guard shall establish and maintain a military engineering body known as Engineers. This body shall be subordinate and answerable to Command Group, or any other administrative entity supervising the body, who shall appoint a Senior Officer, hereinafter referred to as "Engineer Commanding Officer," to oversee and direct a military engineering body.
Engineers shall be the military engineering branch of the Mayflower National Guard.

(a) Engineers shall be tasked with the assembly and maintenance of structures, deployment and disposal of explosive ordnance, utilizing explosive ordnance in the protection of the State of Mayflower and providing civil works.
"Engineers" shall be defined as guardsmen who hold the necessary accreditation and have undergone training to perform their duty.
"Engineer Officers" shall be defined as Commissioned Officers who hold the necessary accreditation and have undergone training to perform their duty.
This subchapter shall only apply during peacetime, outside of an activation of the Guard by the Governor as prescribed by the Constitution.
Engineers shall operate in any place where the Mayflower National Guard are operating from or based, including locality surrounding serving members of the Guard.
(a) This shall not be limited to overseas.
Engineers shall be given permanent jurisdiction within the state which their services and assistance for visible civil works missions that include—
(a) planning, designing, building and operating locks and dams, which includes flood control, beach nourishment and dredging for waterway navigation;
(b) design and construct fortifications and peace lines within civilian areas when deemed necessary to ensure public safety;

(c) design and construct checkpoints, roadblocks or any other form of temporary traffic control system at the request of law enforcement officers with the relevant authority to conduct such operations; and
(d) environmental regulation and ecosystem restoration.
Engineers shall reserve the privilege to request Military Police or any other available guardsmen to assist with the physical security of civil work project sites.
Engineers may only have jurisdiction stipulated in this if they are clearly identifiable as members of the Mayflower National Guard
Engineers shall hold the jurisdiction to render inoperable and adequately dispose of all explosive ordnances that have been placed or stockpiled.

records.text: No individual may be appointed or promoted to the rank of General Officer in the Mayflower National Guard without the following requirements:
(a) At least six (6) consecutive months of service, with no disciplinary action taken against them.
(b) At least two (2) consecutive months of service as a Senior Officer, at the rank of Major or above.
(c) A letter of recommendation from the Adjutant General to the Governor, endorsing the individual's promotion to the rank of General Officer.

No individual may be appointed or promoted to the rank of General Officer in the Mayflower National Guard without first being nominated by the Governor and subsequently receiving a confirmation by a majority of the State Senate.
In the event of a vacancy requiring temporary assignment, the Governor may designate an acting general officer for a period to not exceed seven (7) days pending Senate review.
(a) The Governor shall not designate the same individual as an acting general officer more than once in any single calendar month.
No individual shall exercise the duties or privileges of a general officer, including operational command authority, access to sensitive command briefings, without Senate confirmation.
Any actions taken in violation of this section shall be deemed null and void.

The Mayflower National Guard shall establish and maintain a ceremonial unit known as the Honor Guard, tasked with rendering honors at official events and state functions, safeguarding designated sites, and upholding ceremonial drill proficiency.
The Honor Guard shall be authorized to perform the following duties:
(a) Performing ceremonial functions at state and military events;
(b) Escorting protectees as designated by the Adjutant General or his designee;
(c) Representing the State of Mayflower in intergovernmental or commemorative events;
(d) Protecting designated sites, as defined by 3 M.S.C. 4 § 1121;
(e) The governor may issue ceremonial orders expanding or modifying the scope of authorized events.
The Honor Guard shall have standing permission to access and operate within the designated areas as defined by 3 M.S.C. 4 § 1121.

records.text: The term 'Port Authority' shall refer to:

(a) A governmental or quasi-governmental entity established by statute or through intergovernmental agreement, responsible for the administration, regulation, and security of one or more seaports, harbors or rail terminals not operated by a business entity subject ot the Class I Railway Act;
(b) The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit.
The ‘Commissioner’ shall be defined as the head of the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit.
The ‘Executive Director’ shall be defined as the deputy head of the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit.
The ‘Commissioners Board’ shall be defined as the central command for the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit, as designated by the Commissioner and Executive Director.
The term 'on-duty operator' for the purposes of this subtitle shall refer to persons that are on the Port Authority team in-game and actively working or representing the Port Authority.
The term ‘Port of Entry’ shall refer to any property listed under 6 M.S.C. 5 § 1101.

The term ‘Emergency Management’ shall refer to the Office of Emergency Management, the subordinate entity to the Port Authority responsible for the immediate response and coordination of emergencies on Port Authority facilities.

The term Office of the Inspector General, for the purposes of this subtitle, shall refer to the Office of the Inspector General, the subordinate entity to the Port Authority responsible for general internal investigation and audit.

The term ‘Port Authority Trans Henry’, or PATH, shall refer to the Port Authority Trans Henry Railroad, the subordinate entity of the Port Authority responsible for the upkeep and oversight of railroads and train operations owned by the Port Authority.
In this subtitle, ‘Port Authority Installation’ refers to any of the properties below:
(a) The Lander Marine Terminal;
(b) The International Commerce Center;
(c) Any bridge and tunnel within the State of Mayflower;
(d) The Standish Tunnel Command.

The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, may impose temporary restrictions on the possession or carrying of firearms within Port Authority Installations. Such restrictions shall not exceed a continuous duration of two (2) calendar days.

(a) The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, shall be required to issue a written notice detailing any firearm restrictions no less than thirty (30) minutes prior to such restrictions taking effect. The notice must explicitly specify which categories or types of firearms are subject to restriction.

(b) The provisions of this section shall not apply to on-duty law enforcement officers, military personnel, or other individuals or organizations expressly authorized in writing by the Commissioner or their designee. Such written authorization must identify, with specificity, the organizations or classes of individuals exempted under this subtitle.
(c) Individuals who are found in violation of the written notice, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1201, can be subject to arrest or prosecution under 1 M.S.C. § 6302.

The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, may impose temporary entrance restrictions on any installations, as defined by 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110, for no longer than two (2) calendar days.

(a) The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, may only impose temporary entrance restrictions when notified of a credible threat which compromises the safety of individuals or property within the installation.

(b) The Commissioner, or their designee, or in the event there is no Commissioner present; the highest ranking officer, shall be required to issue a written notice less than thirty (30) minutes prior to such restrictions taking effect.
(c) This statute shall not apply to installations identified under 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110(a) without the express written consent of the Secretary of Transportation.
No individual shall host any event, public gathering, or similar activity on any Port Authority Installation without the express written authorization of the Commissioner or their designee.
(a) This provision shall not apply to official state functions when expressly designated as such by the Governor.
(b) Individuals who are found in violation of the written notice, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1201, can be subject to arrest or prosecution under 1 M.S.C. § 3205.

(c) Individuals found to be in violation of this statute may, at the direction of the Commissioner or their designee, be prohibited from accessing Port Authority Installations, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110(a) and 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110(b), for a period not to exceed one (1) week.

(i) The Commissioner, or their designee, shall be required to issue written notice of such prohibition no less than one (1) hour prior to its implementation. Said notice must clearly specify the duration of the prohibition and the exact date and time at which it shall expire.
A maximum speed limit of thirty (30) studs per second shall be enforced within the Lander Marine Terminal.
The Port Authority Police Department may serve as Commercial vehicle officers, as defined in 6 M.S.C. 1 § 2201, on any Port Authority Installation.

The Office of Emergency Management shall be established as a coordinating authority responsible for preparing, responding to, and recovering from emergencies, disasters, or major incidents affecting any Port Authority Installation or operation.
The Office of Emergency Management shall be obligated to perform the following duties:
(a) Developing and maintaining emergency operations plans.
(b) Conducting interaagency training, public safety drills, and readiness assessments.
(c) Coordinating directly with civilian, state, and federal authorities during emergencies.
(d) Issuance of emergency directives, in coordination with the Commissioners Board.
The Office of the Inspector General shall be established as the independent investigative and auditing agency for all Port Authority personnel and internal operations.
(a) The Office of Inspector General shall have authority to conduct administrative investigations, audits, and compliance reviews;
(b) The Office of Inspector General may issue reports, refer findings for disciplinary or criminal prosecution, and recommend policy changes;
(c) The Office of Inspector General shall have unrestricted access to all documents, systems and personnel under the Port Authority’s jurisdiction;

(d) The Commissioner, or their designee, may establish internal policies that impose restrictions or limitations on the operations, personnel, or investigative scope of the Office of Inspector General, provided such policies do not obstruct ongoing investigations or compromise the Office’s statutory independence.
The Tunnel and Bridge Commission is established to oversee fire safety, rescue services, and emergency preparedness for all bridges, tunnels, and enclosed infrastructure under the Port Authority.
The Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall be obligated to perform the following duties:
(a) The Commission shall maintain trained firefighting and rescue personnel;
(b) The Commission shall ensure readiness of firefighting apparatus and emergency vehicles at all crossings;
(c) The Commission shall coordinate with local fire departments in mutual aid operations;
(d) The Commission may impose safety regulations and inspection protocols specific to Port Authority Installations, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110.
The Port Authority shall incorporate a sub-agency (hereinafter “Port Authority Public Safety”) which shall serve as a protective entity of the Port Authority and it’s installations.
Port Authority Public Safety shall:
(a) Port Authority Public Safety shall provide security to properties and assets maintained fully or in part by or under the purview of the Port Authority, as defined in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110;
(b) Not hold peace office status nor be classified as private security officers. However, shall:

(i) Be granted the powers, authorities and privileges afforded to private security officers under the Security Services Act. This includes but is not limited to being designated as an ‘authorized officer’;

Port Authority Public Safety shall only be authorized to hire individuals who presently hold a valid Security License that has been issued by the Department of State, in accordance with 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1304.
Port Authority Public Safety officers shall maintain a budget of no more than forty (40) personnel, as prescribed by 3 M.S.C. 1 § 2213.

The Commissioner, or their designee, shall be permitted to enter into contracts with Private Patrol Operators to assist in protection of Port Authority Installations, as prescribed in 3 M.S.C. 5 § 1110, at their discretion.
(a) Contracts must remain publicly accessibly throughout their duration.
